title: Trump Used Truth Social as De Facto Presidential Bulletin Channel
description_short: Trump Used Truth Social as De Facto Presidential Bulletin Channel
description_medium: The Guardian described Truth Social as an unofficial presidential mouthpiece during Trump's second term, highlighting how policy signals increasingly flowed through a platform with limited audience share and weak guardrails. This communication model shifts state messaging from institutional channels toward owner-controlled media space, increasing risk of impulsive framing and reducing traditional review friction.
description_long:
During his second term, Donald Trump has used Truth Social for presidential communications, including announcements of broad tariffs and major military operations, according to NBC News. The report contrasted those posts with earlier presidents’ reliance on formal channels such as the White House press office and its website. Truth Social therefore became a prominent route for statements about economic policy and international affairs, even though it is a privately owned platform.

The platform’s role also acquired a commercial dimension. In August 2026, Trump Media and Technology Group launched Truth API, a paid feed that gives subscribing firms real-time alerts for posts by Trump and other accounts. NBC reported that firms might receive alerts milliseconds before general users, a potential advantage for high-frequency trading. Trump held a 41% stake in the company, according to his 2025 financial disclosure, and Senators Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff called for an SEC investigation. The report documents the official-message role and the business interests around faster access; it does not resolve whether the proposed feed violated securities rules.

notes: Completed using NBC News reporting on tariff and military announcements posted to Truth Social, the Truth API feed, and the company ownership disclosed in 2025.

title: Trump’s Iran Media Push Turned Foreign Policy Into a Domestic Narrative Battlefield
description_short: Trump’s Iran Media Push Turned Foreign Policy Into a Domestic Narrative Battlefield
description_medium: AP’s reporting showed Trump folding an active conflict into domestic identity combat, where support for strikes became a proxy test of personal loyalty. That framing compresses complex policy into tribal signaling and makes correction harder once facts change. The result was a foreign-policy discussion increasingly run as campaign rhetoric under wartime conditions.

title: Trump Turned Negotiation Ambiguity Into an Escalation Lever Before Iran Strikes
description_short: Trump Turned Negotiation Ambiguity Into an Escalation Lever Before Iran Strikes
description_medium: AP's reconstructed timeline showed Trump repeatedly amplifying uncertainty around diplomacy before authorizing force. That sequence matters because ambiguity can be used as an escalation lever when leaders want action while preserving rhetorical deniability. In practice, Trump made uncertainty itself part of decision architecture, compressing debate and making off-ramps harder to defend publicly.
